tools.name: lookup_hash
tools.description: Find analyses of a known SHA-256 digest. Returns the caller's own scans of those bytes plus any publicly shared scan of them. Sends nothing anywhere: this searches scans that already exist on this platform. Answers with an empty list when the hash is unknown or not visible to this token, without dis

tools.name: get_report
tools.description: The derived analysis report for one scan: verdict, capabilities, behaviour summary, observed operations and defanged indicators. Derived data only - it never contains the sample's bytes, its decompiled source, a download link or an artifact reference. Every list in the result reports what was return

tools.name: search_indicator
tools.description: Find scans where an indicator was observed: an IP, a domain, a URL, a mutex, a registry key, a hash or a JA3/JA4 fingerprint. The indicator is matched exactly; defanged input such as 'evil[.]com' is refanged first. Only scans this token may read are searched.

tools.name: poll_scan
tools.description: The current status of one scan, for polling after submit_scan. Cheap enough to call in a loop. 'terminal' means the scan will not change again; 'report_available' means get_report will return a full report. Answers 'not found' for an unknown scan and an unreadable one identically.

tools.name: submit_scan
tools.description: Queue a new analysis of a target that can be named as text: a SHA-256 to look up, a URL to visit, a command to run, or a package to install. findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_indicator, submit_scan · Private data: lookup_hash, get_report, search_indicator, submit_scan · Public sink: submit_scan · Destructive: submit_scan.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_indicator, submit_scan · Private data: lookup_hash, get_report, search_indicator, submit_scan · Public sink: submit_scan · Destructive: submit_scan

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
